title: Payroll tax calculation: how gross pay becomes net pay | Omnia.tax
description: How payroll tax is calculated, step by step: FICA wage base ($184,500 in 2026), federal and state withholding, unemployment tax, a worked example.
h1: Payroll tax calculation, step by step

faq.q: How do you calculate payroll taxes?
faq.a: Start with gross pay, subtract the deductions that are pre-tax for each tax, then apply each tax to its own taxable wages: Social Security at 6.2% up to the wage base, Medicare at 1.45%, federal income tax from the employee's Form W-4, then state and local tax. Employers add federal and state unemployment tax on top.

faq.q: What is the Social Security wage base?
faq.a: $184,500 for 2026 and $192,300 for 2027. Social Security tax stops once an employee's wages for the year pass that amount; Medicare has no cap.

faq.q: Is a 401(k) deferral subject to payroll tax?
faq.a: It depends on the tax. A traditional 401(k) deferral reduces federal and most state income tax wages, but it is still subject to Social Security and Medicare. That difference between taxes is the most common cause of payroll tax errors.

faq.q: Can an API calculate payroll taxes for me?
faq.a: Yes. Omnia.tax takes earnings, deductions, a Form W-4, year-to-date wages and the work location, and returns each tax line with the wages it applied to and who pays it. It calculates; you still file and deposit.

title: Payroll tax API: federal, state, local | Omnia.tax
description: A payroll tax calculation API for developers: federal, state, local and employer taxes in one request. JSON in cents, OpenAPI spec, $0.08 per paycheck.

faq.q: What is a payroll tax API?
faq.a: An HTTP service that takes one paycheck (earnings, deductions, the employee's W-4 and work location) and returns the payroll taxes: federal, state and local withholding, Social Security, Medicare and the employer taxes.

faq.q: How much does the Omnia.tax payroll tax API cost?
faq.a: $0.08 per paycheck calculation after a 14-day free trial. There are no seat fees.

faq.q: Does Omnia.tax file or pay payroll taxes?
faq.a: No. It calculates the tax. It does not file returns, deposit or remit tax, pay employees or move money, and it does not give tax advice.

faq.q: Which states and years does it cover?
faq.a: All 50 states and DC for 2025, 2026 and 2027 (2027 is provisional where a state has not yet published its tables), plus local taxes in 15 states covering 4,140 jurisdictions and 69 local minimum wage ordinances.

title: Symmetry Tax Engine alternative: payroll tax API | Omnia.tax
description: Comparing Symmetry Tax Engine with Omnia.tax: what each covers, how each is sold, and when a self-serve payroll tax API is and is not a fit.

faq.q: Is Omnia.tax a Symmetry Tax Engine alternative?
faq.a: For some teams. If you need a self-serve HTTP API for gross-to-net payroll tax with public per-call pricing and you can work with state-level coverage plus the local taxes listed on our coverage page, it can replace a tax engine. If you need Symmetry's breadth of local jurisdictions, withholding forms, I-9 or a vendor with decades of production history, it is not a like-for-like replacement.

faq.q: Is the Omnia.tax API compatible with Symmetry's?
faq.a: No. Omnia.tax has an adapter that accepts a Symmetry-shaped payCalc request, but it is not wire-compatible with Symmetry's API, and its tax jurisdiction ids are its own, not Symmetry's. Expect to change your integration.

faq.q: How is Omnia.tax priced compared with Symmetry?
faq.a: Omnia.tax is $0.08 per paycheck calculation after a 14-day trial, published on the pricing page. Symmetry does not publish a price on its website; it directs buyers to a demo. We have not seen Symmetry's pricing and do not compare it.

title: Payroll tax engine comparison: Symmetry, Vertex, Check, Omnia.tax
description: Compare payroll tax calculation options: Symmetry Tax Engine, Vertex Payroll Tax, Check, a self-serve API, or build it yourself. What each covers.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Symmetry Software?
faq.a: Other ways to get payroll tax calculation include Vertex Payroll Tax, an embedded payroll API such as Check, a self-serve payroll tax API such as Omnia.tax, or building the rules in-house from IRS and state publications. Which fits depends on whether you need only calculation or a full payroll platform.

faq.q: Should I build payroll tax calculation myself?
faq.a: Only if payroll tax is your product. The arithmetic is simple. Keeping every state and local rule current, effective-dated and tested is the permanent cost.
